name: How much does a whole-house remodel cost in Los Angeles for a 1,500 to 2,000 square foot home?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for a whole-house remodel in Los Angeles if my home is around 1,500 to 2,000 square feet?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget for a whole-house remodel in Los Angeles if my home is around 1,500 to 2,000 square feet?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 1,500 to 2,000 square foot Los Angeles home, a true whole-house remodel usually starts well above a cosmetic refresh. The biggest cost drivers are whether the project is a partial update or a full gut renovation, whether walls move, and whether major systems are replaced. Kitchen and bath scope, cabinetry grade, tile, flooring, windows, HVAC, and electrical panel upgrades can move the budget dramatically. Homeowners should expect a wide range because labor, permitting, and material selection vary by neighborhood and project complexity. A realistic budget should include design fees, engineering, permit costs, temporary living expenses, and a contingency reserve for hidden conditions like old plumbing, framing issues, or asbestos. In higher-end areas and for luxury finishes, the total can climb well beyond typical regional averages. The safest approach is to define must-have scope first, then request a detailed line-item estimate. That makes it easier to compare bids and identify where value engineering is possible without sacrificing quality.
acceptedAnswer.description: A whole-house remodel in Los Angeles for a 1,500 to 2,000 square foot home often lands in the mid-six-figure range when it includes kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, electrical, plumbing, and finish upgrades. Costs rise quickly with layout changes, structural work, permits, and custom materials.
